data.why: the repo ships nine real gravel-pack screen inspection photos plus hand-labelled ground truth, and the dashboard reads results from the SQLite DB the batch pipeline writes from those images, so no external data is needed

goals: review the campaign dashboard to see which screens show the highest erosion % and most defects
open the review queue and triage the detections the classifier flagged below its confidence threshold, approving or rejecting each
drill into a single image's analysis page to inspect severity, dominant failure type, and the morphological reasoning behind a classification
tag images with well name and completion zone in the gallery and compare erosion across screens from the same well
calibrate pixels-per-mm on an image to convert diameters and areas into physical units
export a per-image or campaign-summary PDF engineering report for the inspection record

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree: its five phases match the README's triage / browse / drill-down / compare / report organisation, labels are clean at both levels, and all ten screens I checked show what their nodes claim. It needs small fixes before filing: record that the view mode does not persist across pages, settle the unconfirmed hand-pick comparison, and recut two features (split CSV export from PDF download, and extract the shared comparison panel).
